newsitem.title: FRANCE: "France can't afford to change direction"-Chirac.
newsitem.headline: "France can't afford to change direction"-Chirac.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac said on Wednesday that France could not affort to change direction without taking risks, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said.
He said Chirac told the last cabinet meeting before next Sunday's decisive parliamentary runoff: "France cannot afford to change direction all the time without taking serious risks".
Chirac urged centre-right ministers to explain to voters that "in the next five years, France must be government in a modern, coherent and determined way".

The left-wing opposition outpolled the centre-right coalition by more than four points in last Sunday's first round of voting and polling institutes said it was on course for a narrow majority if the voting pattern were repeated in Sunday's runoff.

Chirac said the work done by outgoing Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who has announced he will resign whatever the election result, had enabled the country to face the next stage of its development "in good conditions".
To change direction now would lead the country into "confusion and weakness", Lamassoure quoted him as saying.
